01 / REFLECTOR

Lower = deeper bowl. Higher = shallower bowl.

10–15° change between two planar rear faces. The front stays parabolic. Thickness sets the minimum vertical wall; corners grow thicker. Solid CAD volume is not a filament estimate—choose infill in your slicer.

02 / JOINTS & CENTER

Four bolts clamp each seam. 8 mm locating tongues enter reinforced rear sockets, resisting slip and rotation. Rear-installed fittings allow the last petal to drop into place.

New matching kit required. Indexed center: flat back, 60 mm mount bolt circle, slimmer front clamp. Start with one joint to tune fit.

PRINT ORIENTATION & SUPPORTS

Keyed joints, faceted backs, or ribs prefer a 60° diagonal petal. Bed rotation minimizes the fitting footprint.

Orange ribs are disposable. Choose a ridge width your nozzle can print; calibrate the vertical gap for your material and layer height.

Segmentation & tolerances

Mesh spacing controls tessellation, not printer layer height. Smaller spacing increases file size.

From geometry to a first fit check

1 / Print one joint first

Start with one panel and its supports. Angled petals keep their concave faces away from the ribs. With ribs enabled, the petal is lifted 5.6 mm while flared rib feet sit at Z = 0. Automatic orientation checks angles and bed rotation; hub and bridge parts retain their low-profile orientation.

2 / Slice the supported petal

Keep the STL as one object, with all shells in their original positions. Disable automatic supports for the petal after checking the layer preview. Do not drop the petal separately to the bed or auto-arrange its ribs. Print a single test first; the rib contact gap is vertical CAD clearance, not a slicer support setting. Hubs and joint bridges may still need slicer supports.

3 / Assemble from the center

Place the inner panel roots on the rear hub. Seat the petal roots on the hub’s locating shoulders. Add the front clamp loosely, then outer rings. Install saddles from behind; their four tongues seat in matching sockets. Tighten gradually with washers.

4 / Preserve the surface

Use the cross-section to check the shape after assembly. The CAD thickness is vertical, not normal to the surface. Keyed joints add 3 mm rear docking pads; their sockets stop before the original shell, preserving its thickness. Two-facet mode preserves a parabolic front and adds a variable-thickness rear, with a 10–15° fold. Petals remain diagonal; backing brackets get a flat base. Bolt heads and clamp sit above the front surface. A reflector finish must account for seams, fasteners, and center opening.

5 / Adapt the mount

The rear hub uses a custom four-hole M4 pattern, clocked at 45°. Keyed mounts use a 60 mm bolt circle; legacy mounts use 40 mm. It is not a tripod thread or a commercial antenna standard. Regenerate the full kit when the joint system or geometry changes. Feed supports are not included.

Geometric fit includes enabled ribs. Angle selection is a fit heuristic, not a strength or print-reliability simulation. Socket clearance, contact settings, stiffness, assembly fit, and reflector performance need physical validation. Large shells may need additional bracing. Use OpenSCAD to adapt the design: official syntax reference. Support-gap guidance: Prusa support settings.
